newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani opposition to step up anti-Bhutto drive.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani opposition to step up anti-Bhutto drive.

text.p: Pakistani opposition leader Nawaz Sharif said on Tuesday his Pakistan Muslim League (PML) party would step up its campaign to oust Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto.

Speaking at a news conference after a meeting of the PML parliamentary group, he rejected Bhutto's repeated offers of talks to settle differences on national issues, including proposed constitutional amendments the prime minister wants for political reforms.
But he said the two sides could work together if the government agreed to early fresh elections under a neutral interim government.

"If the government announces the election date today, we are ready to do everything in cooperation with the government, including constitutional amendments," he said. "But we can't trust this government."
Bhutto says she will not step down before completing her five-year term in October 1998.

Sharif said his party had requisitioned a new session of the National Assembly (lower house) to decide on setting up a commission to punish corrupt politicians and was also preparing a corruption petition against some government functionaries to be moved before a superior court.

He said the PML had sought a new session because the regular assembly session was prorogued on Monday without taking a decision on his demand the government set up a commission of senior judges to probe into the conduct of politicians.

Bhutto denies corruption charges and accuses opposition politicians of campaigning against her to escape prosecution for their own alleged wrongdoings committed when Sharif was prime minister for 32 months until July 1993.
The government does not want a new commission, saying existing forums were adequate to deal with complaints.

Sharif accused Bhutto's government of trying to avoid facing charges of corruption and mismanagement, which he said had damaged Pakistan's economy and was responsible for the present slide of the Pakistani rupee and the stock market.
"The common man is crying (because of economic difficulties) and fears are being expressed of a possible run on banks and default in debt repayment," he said.
"The hands who brought the country to this pass must be punished. We want dirty faces to be exposed before the nation. We want dirty faces out of the political field."
The PML is the moving force in a 14-party "Pakistan Bachao" (Save Pakistan) grouping that has begun a campaign of public rallies to force Bhutto to step down.
Sharif said the next rally in the campaign had been set for October 7 at Lahore, his home town and capital of the populous Punjab province.
